acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW under sustained 2x-capacity overrun: tail records dropped, head records preserved, dropped-count metric > 0, no producer deadlock
DROP_OLD under sustained 2x-capacity overrun: oldest records evicted, newest records preserved, eviction-count metric > 0, no producer deadlock
BLOCK under sustained overrun: producer parks until consumer catches up, zero data loss, total delivered equals total sent, park releases within 2x configured timeout

OVERFLOW_TO_DISK under sustained overrun: spill file created at <tempdir>/dag-spill-<partitionId>-<edgeId>.spill, all records preserved in arrival order, drain reads back every record in FIFO order, spill file deleted after drain
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK partial drain readback: interrupt drain mid-way; already-drained messages not re-delivered on resume
Hot-swap DROP_NEW to OVERFLOW_TO_DISK mid-run: no data corruption, no stale spill file leak, records spilled before swap drain correctly
Hot-swap BLOCK to DROP_NEW mid-stream: no deadlock, producer unblocks within one drain cycle, subsequent messages follow DROP_NEW semantics
Stale spill file on startup: orphaned .spill file triggers IllegalStateException before partition starts, no silent replay
Corrupted spill CRC/invariant failure mid-drain: MmapJournal CRC or length invariant failure surfaces as explicit exception, not silent data loss or partial replay
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK failure/partial write: process interrupted mid-spill write; on restart MmapJournal journal recovery delivers only fully-written entries, no phantom messages
jmhSmokeCheck allocation gate: no heap regression on DROP_NEW/DROP_OLD hot path when queue is not full; zero per-event object allocations confirmed by JMH allocation benchmark
qa/smoke.sh exits 0 after all slices land
qa/regression.sh exits 0 with no regressions in existing GraphPartitionRunner test suite
GraphPartitionRunnerJoinEpochIsolationTest: no regression
assumptions: MmapJournal is expected to be present in dag-framework-lvc/src/main/java/ from lvc-standard; the design slice must confirm MmapJournal API signatures (append/drain/close) are available and sufficient for spill use before qa-author writes spill tests; if MmapJournal is absent or unstable, impl-overflow-spill must be blocked and escalated to human before proceeding.
GraphPartitionRunner holds a per-partition lock that can be extended to guard policy-read and queue-mutation atomically.
GraphPartitionRunner.Builder is the sole public entry point for per-edge policy configuration; no framework-internal edge wiring bypasses it.
Per-edge policy config fits naturally as a field on the existing edge/node descriptor in SimpleGraphDefinitionBuilder alongside JoinPolicy.
Spill files are ephemeral: created per-edge per-partition on overflow, drained FIFO on consumer catch-up, deleted on clean close; no cross-restart durability is required.
Hot-swap is edge-scoped and atomic at the edge level; in-flight spill files complete their drain before a new policy takes effect.
jmhSmokeCheck benchmarks exist and are run via qa/smoke.sh; allocation gate is enforced by an existing JMH allocation threshold assertion.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh are the authoritative gate scripts and their exit codes are the source of truth for CI.
No custom policy extension points, priority-based shedding, or cross-partition backpressure propagation are in scope.

critic.rationale:
The plan is structurally sound across all 17 rubric checks. It carries a full design_contract with explicit persistence_protocol (MmapJournal-backed spill, FIFO drain, stale-file guard) and concurrency_protocol (AtomicReference CAS under per-partition lock, bounded-park BLOCK, drain-before-swap hot-swap guard). All four acceptance-matrix lifecycle cases are present: stale/invalid (stale spill file -> IllegalStateException), invariant (CRC/length failure -> explicit exception), and failure/partial (partial-write recovery via MmapJournal journal recovery). The topology is split_specialists, which is compatible with two implementer slices. Dependency chain is linear and non-orphaned: design -> qa-author -> impl-policy-core -> impl-overflow-spill -> review -> qa-verify. All implementer and QA slices carry qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh verification commands. QA allowed paths are strictly test trees and stay disjoint from implementer source allowed paths. finalization_policy is open_final_feature_pr_for_human_merge. Risk register is present with 11 entries covering the principal failure modes. Roadmap entry carries no prerequisites (Depends on: none), so no blocking/sequencing is required. Allocation gate is covered by jmhSmokeCheck hard constraint, risk register entry, and BackpressureAllocationBenchmark expected output in qa-verify; no slice schedules allocation-introducing work on the hot path without the gate test in place. The feature touches seven distinct surfaces (api, runtime-core, lvc, benchmarks, fixtures, docs, repo-memory), has four policies, hot-swap, and mmap spill mechanics — split_specialists with six slices is proportionate.

One structural defect flagged by the validator: the review slice carries empty forbidden_paths. While no rubric check strictly requires forbidden_paths on a reviewer slice (the overlap check only fires when both lists are non-empty and intersect), the empty forbidden_paths means the review role carries no write-boundary guard, allowing it to write to production source paths. This is captured as an advisory finding under check_slice_path_coverage and check_forbidden_path_overlap — both technically pass by rubric definition (there is no overlap between an empty set and anything), but the absence is noted. The runtime validator has separately emitted a hard error on this condition; the plan should add a forbidden_paths list to the review slice before the verdict is computed.

critic.rationale: The plan is well-structured across all 17 rubric dimensions. design_contract carries explicit persistence_protocol (MmapJournal backend, spill path template, FIFO drain, deletion, maxSpillBytes enforcement, stale-file guard) and concurrency_protocol (AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> CAS hot-swap within partition lock, bounded BLOCK park, per-edge drain serialization, drain-before-switch guard). All 11 affected_surfaces map to at least one slice's allowed_paths. No slice contains an entry that appears in both its own allowed_paths and forbidden_paths. Every implementer and both QA slices carry verification commands (qa/smoke.sh and/or qa/regression.sh). The acceptance_test_matrix covers stale spill on startup, CRC/length invariant failure, and failure/partial-write recovery — satisfying the three lifecycle sub-cases. topology is split_specialists with two implementer slices, which is compatible (SINGLE topology would be the violation). A reviewer slice (engineering.review) is present. engineering.qa.author precedes both implementers in the dependency chain. engineering.qa.verify follows the review slice. QA author/verify allowed paths are strictly in src/test/ and qa/fixtures/ trees, fully disjoint from implementer src/main/ paths. Every non-terminal slice is consumed by a downstream slice; no orphans exist. finalization_policy is open_final_feature_pr_for_human_merge, keeping merge human-gated. All slice objectives name concrete files, test class names, method signatures, and metrics. The risk_register carries 12 explicit entries. R-006 has no external roadmap dependencies ('Depends on: none'); the MmapJournal soft dependency is sequenced internally via the design slice gate. The zero-allocation hard constraint is stated in design_contract.hard_constraints, enforced by the jmhSmokeCheck acceptance gate, and repeated in impl-policy-core's objective — no scheduled work violates it. R-006 spans 11 affected surfaces with four policy variants, mmap I/O integration, and hot-swap; 6 slices under split_specialists topology is proportionate and not excessive for this complexity.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge carries an AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> for hot-swap; swap is a single CAS. Queue-length check and policy dispatch execute under the existing per-partition lock to prevent torn reads. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free reads against queue capacity within the partition lock scope. BLOCK policy uses the partition lock's Condition to park the producer thread; a bounded park timeout (configurable, default 100 ms) prevents indefinite deadlock; BLOCK must not share a lock with the consumer read path. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes and drain through a per-edge lock; drain holds the partition lock and blocks concurrent appends. Hot-swap waits for any active spill drain to complete before activating the new policy.
forbidden_alternatives: New or custom spill file format bypassing MmapJournal.
Global (non-per-edge) policy applied uniformly without Builder opt-in.
Cross-partition backpressure signaling.
Priority queues or weighted shedding inside DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
Persistent spill recovery across JVM restarts.
Custom policy SPI or user-supplied BackpressurePolicy implementations.
Mutable EdgeBackpressureConfig fields mutated in place for hot-swap.
Merging BackpressurePolicy into the existing JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy enums.
hard_constraints: Reuse MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc for all spill I/O; do not invent a new binary format.
Allocation gate (jmhSmokeCheck) must remain green; no per-event heap allocation on the hot path for DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, or BLOCK when queue is not full.
No custom policy extension point (no BackpressurePolicy interface or SPI beyond the four specified values).
No priority-based shedding within DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
No cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Hot-swap must not lose records already committed to the spill file; drain completes before the new policy activates.
EdgeBackpressureConfig must be immutable; policy hot-swap goes through setEdgeBackpressure only.
BackpressurePolicy must be a standalone enum; do not merge with JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy.
BLOCK policy must not share a lock with the consumer read path to avoid deadlock.

MmapJournal API availability in dag-framework-lvc must be confirmed by the design slice before impl-overflow-spill proceeds; if absent or unstable, escalate to human before starting spill implementation.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns BackpressurePolicy enum and EdgeBackpressureConfig value type with no runtime imports. runtime-core owns per-edge policy enforcement, DROP/BLOCK queue-overflow dispatch, spill lifecycle, and hot-swap implementation. dag-framework-lvc MmapJournal is consumed read-only by runtime-core via a MmapSpillAdapter wrapper; no modifications to dag-framework-lvc internals. QA write paths own all test fixtures, failing tests, and regression scripts exclusively.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK uses MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc as the spill backend. Spill file path: <tempdir>/dag-spill-<partitionId>-<edgeId>.spill. Journal is append-only during overflow; drained in arrival order (FIFO) when the edge queue drops below half-capacity. Spill file is deleted via MmapJournal.close() after full drain. EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes is enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter. No cross-restart recovery; a stale spill file on startup triggers IllegalStateException before partition starts, not silent replay.

GraphPartitionRunner.Builder gains edgeBackpressure(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy policy) and edgeBackpressure(String edgeId, EdgeBackpressureConfig config). Running runner exposes setEdgeBackpressure(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy policy) for hot-swap.

GraphPartitionRunner holds a per-partition lock that can be extended to guard policy-read and queue-mutation atomically.

Hot-swap is edge-scoped and atomic at the edge level; in-flight spill files complete their drain before a new policy takes effect.
jmhSmokeCheck benchmarks exist and are run via qa/smoke.sh; allocation gate is enforced by an existing JMH allocation threshold assertion.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh are the authoritative gate scripts and their exit codes are the source of truth for CI.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge carries an AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> for hot-swap; swap is a single CAS. Queue-length check and policy dispatch execute under the existing per-partition lock to prevent torn reads. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free reads against queue capacity within the partition lock scope. BLOCK policy uses the partition lock's Condition to park the producer thread; a bounded park timeout (configurable, default 100 ms) prevents indefinite deadlock; BLOCK must not share a lock with the consumer read path. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes and drain through a per-edge lock; drain holds the partition lock and blocks concurrent appends. Hot-swap waits for any active spill drain to complete before activating the new policy.

Hot-swap CAS between policy-read and queue-mutation under concurrent producer threads may allow one record to observe stale policy; mitigation: AtomicReference read and queue dispatch must be within the same partition lock critical section.

BLOCK policy deadlock if consumer never catches up or consumer and producer share a thread pool; mitigation: bounded park with timeout (default 100 ms) and dropped-block metric; document thread-safety contract; test explicitly on separate threads in qa-author.

MmapJournal close race if hot-swap fires while drain is in progress; mitigation: hot-swap guard waits for active drain to complete before switching policy.

Spill file not cleaned up on abnormal partition close (OOM, uncaught exception); mitigation: try-finally in partition lifecycle; reviewer must confirm cleanup path is covered by the OVERFLOW_TO_DISK failure/partial-write acceptance test.

Unbounded spill file growth if drain rate is permanently below fill rate; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter.

MmapJournal API version mismatch between lvc-standard pinned in dag-framework-lvc and the spill adapter call sites; mitigation: compile-time module dependency on dag-framework-lvc; integration test in qa-verify will surface API breakage.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK spill directory not writable at runtime; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig validation at Builder.build() must throw IllegalArgumentException for non-writable spillDir.

critic.rationale:
The plan is structurally sound across all 17 rubric checks. It carries a full design_contract with explicit persistence_protocol (MmapJournal-backed spill, FIFO drain, stale-file guard) and concurrency_protocol (AtomicReference CAS under per-partition lock, bounded-park BLOCK, drain-before-swap hot-swap guard). All four acceptance-matrix lifecycle cases are present: stale/invalid (stale spill file -> IllegalStateException), invariant (CRC/length failure -> explicit exception), and failure/partial (partial-write recovery via MmapJournal journal recovery). The topology is split_specialists, which is compatible with two implementer slices. Dependency chain is linear and non-orphaned: design -> qa-author -> impl-policy-core -> impl-overflow-spill -> review -> qa-verify. All implementer and QA slices carry qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh verification commands. QA allowed paths are strictly test trees and stay disjoint from implementer source allowed paths. finalization_policy is open_final_feature_pr_for_human_merge. Risk register is present with 11 entries covering the principal failure modes. Roadmap entry carries no prerequisites (Depends on: none), so no blocking/sequencing is required. Allocation gate is covered by jmhSmokeCheck hard constraint, risk register entry, and BackpressureAllocationBenchmark expected output in qa-verify; no slice schedules allocation-introducing work on the hot path without the gate test in place. The feature touches seven distinct surfaces (api, runtime-core, lvc, benchmarks, fixtures, docs, repo-memory), has four policies, hot-swap, and mmap spill mechanics — split_specialists with six slices is proportionate.

One structural defect flagged by the validator: the review slice carries empty forbidden_paths. While no rubric check strictly requires forbidden_paths on a reviewer slice (the overlap check only fires when both lists are non-empty and intersect), the empty forbidden_paths means the review role carries no write-boundary guard, allowing it to write to production source paths. This is captured as an advisory finding under check_slice_path_coverage and check_forbidden_path_overlap — both technically pass by rubric definition (there is no overlap between an empty set and anything), but the absence is noted. The runtime validator has separately emitted a hard error on this condition; the plan should add a forbidden_paths list to the review slice before the verdict is computed.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free CAS operations on the edge bounded queue. BLOCK uses a single Semaphore per edge acquired by the producer and released by the consumer; no cross-edge locks permitted. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes through a per-edge ReentrantLock; drain is single-threaded per edge. Hot-swap is guarded by a volatile policy reference plus a StampedLock write-stamp to drain in-flight operations before the new policy activates.
forbidden_alternatives: Custom spill format or raw FileChannel writes bypassing MmapJournal.
Global (non-per-edge) policy applied uniformly without Builder opt-in.
Priority queue or weighted-fair shedding inside any policy.
Synchronous cross-partition signal on overrun.
Mutable EdgeBackpressureConfig fields mutated in place for hot-swap.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom policies beyond the four specified.
Do not add priority-based shedding.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Reuse MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc; do not invent a new spill format.
Allocation gate (jmhSmokeCheck) must remain green after this change.
EdgeBackpressureConfig must be immutable (record or final fields); policy hot-swap goes through BackpressurePolicySwitch only.
BLOCK policy must not share a lock with the consumer's read path to avoid deadlock.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns the BackpressurePolicy enum and EdgeBackpressureConfig value type with no runtime imports. runtime-core owns policy dispatch, BLOCK/DROP logic, and the BackpressurePolicySwitch implementation. dag-framework-lvc owns MmapJournal; the spill adapter in runtime-core wraps it via the existing lvc API without modifying lvc internals.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK only. Spill file is a MmapJournal segment rooted at EdgeBackpressureConfig.spillDir / edgeId.spill; written on overrun, drained FIFO on consumer catch-up. File is deleted on clean partition close. No WAL or checksum beyond what MmapJournal already provides.
design_contract.public_api: BackpressurePolicy enum {DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, OVERFLOW_TO_DISK} in dag-framework-api/src/main/; EdgeBackpressureConfig record holding (BackpressurePolicy policy, int capacity, Path spillDir) in dag-framework-api/src/main/; GraphPartitionRunner.Builder.edgePolicy(String edgeId, EdgeBackpressureConfig config) and Builder.globalPolicy(EdgeBackpressureConfig config) in runtime-core/src/main/; BackpressurePolicySwitch.swap(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy next) interface for hot-swap in runtime-core/src/main/.

Hot-swap race between policy reference update and in-flight CAS on the edge queue: mitigated by StampedLock write-stamp draining in-flight operations before activating new policy; hot-swap tests must cover concurrent producer load during swap.

Spill file not cleaned up on abnormal partition close (OOM, uncaught exception): mitigated by try-finally in partition lifecycle; reviewer must confirm cleanup path is covered by failure/partial acceptance test.

candidate.problem_statement: GraphPartitionRunner has no pluggable backpressure mechanism; all edges silently block or drop under sustained overrun with no operator control. R-006 adds DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK policies selectable per-edge via GraphPartitionRunner.Builder, with OVERFLOW_TO_DISK implemented via the existing MmapJournal machinery from dag-framework-lvc.
risk_register: MmapJournal drain API may not expose ordered replay or CRC verification publicly — requires source audit in design slice before impl-overflow-spill begins; mitigation: add minimal package-private bridge if needed, do not fork the format.

Hot-swap from OVERFLOW_TO_DISK to another policy while spill file is partially drained could leave an orphaned mmap file — mitigation: drain must complete fully before policy swap is acknowledged; hot-swap must block briefly or reject the swap with IllegalStateException if drain is in progress.

BLOCK policy deadlock if producer and consumer share a thread (e.g. single-threaded test executor) — mitigation: document thread-safety contract; add a tryOffer timeout overload; test explicitly on separate threads in qa-author.

Unbounded spill file growth if drain rate is permanently below fill rate — mitigation: SpillConfig.maxBytes enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter; test this boundary in qa-author.

Allocation gate regression from mmap buffer allocation during OVERFLOW_TO_DISK init — mitigation: buffer is allocated once at spill-file open, not per event; verify with JMH allocation benchmark in qa-verify.

PartitionPolicy extension point may require a source-incompatible change to accept BackpressurePolicy — mitigation: keep the two enums separate per hard constraint; wire via a parallel edge-config map in GraphPartitionRunner.Builder.

Concurrent hot-swap and spill drain creating a race on the volatile policy field — mitigation: CAS on swap; drain checks policy after each record written and aborts cleanly if policy changed away from OVERFLOW_TO_DISK.

consolidated.problem_statement: GraphPartitionRunner has no per-edge queue-overflow handling; sustained producer overrun silently drops data or deadlocks with no configurable policy. R-006 adds DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK backpressure policies with per-edge configuration and hot-swap, using MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc for spill I/O.
risk_register: MmapJournal prerequisite: MmapJournal is expected to be present in dag-framework-lvc from lvc-standard, but if R-002/snapshot work has not yet merged or the API surface is insufficient, impl-overflow-spill cannot proceed; mitigation: design slice must explicitly confirm MmapJournal append/drain/close API signatures before qa-author writes spill tests; if absent or unstable, escalate to human before impl-overflow-spill starts.
MmapJournal API surface in dag-framework-lvc may not expose append/drain/close at the granularity needed; mitigation: design slice must confirm API fit before qa-author writes tests.

Hot-swap CAS between policy-read and queue-mutation under concurrent producer threads may allow one record to observe stale policy; mitigation: AtomicReference read and queue dispatch must be within the same partition lock critical section.

BLOCK policy deadlock if consumer never catches up or consumer and producer share a thread pool; mitigation: bounded park with timeout (default 100 ms) and dropped-block metric; document thread-safety contract; test explicitly on separate threads in qa-author.

Spill file not deleted on JVM crash leaves stale file on next startup; mitigation: stale file startup guard throws IllegalStateException; register JVM shutdown hook in MmapSpillAdapter to close and unmap the segment; operator must delete manually (no silent replay).

Allocation regression on hot path: spill coordinator instantiation, AtomicReference boxing, or per-edge lock allocation may trigger GC; mitigation: allocate lock objects once at Builder.build() time; allocation gate in jmhSmokeCheck is a hard acceptance gate.
Drain ordering under concurrent append: simultaneous overflow and drain may interleave records; mitigation: drain holds partition lock; appends are blocked during drain.
MmapJournal close race if hot-swap fires while drain is in progress; mitigation: hot-swap guard waits for active drain to complete before switching policy.

Spill file not cleaned up on abnormal partition close (OOM, uncaught exception); mitigation: try-finally in partition lifecycle; reviewer must confirm cleanup path is covered by the OVERFLOW_TO_DISK failure/partial-write acceptance test.

Unbounded spill file growth if drain rate is permanently below fill rate; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter.

MmapJournal API version mismatch between lvc-standard pinned in dag-framework-lvc and the spill adapter call sites; mitigation: compile-time module dependency on dag-framework-lvc; integration test in qa-verify will surface API breakage.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK spill directory not writable at runtime; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig validation at Builder.build() must throw IllegalArgumentException for non-writable spillDir.

critic.rationale: The plan is well-structured across all 17 rubric dimensions. design_contract carries explicit persistence_protocol (MmapJournal backend, spill path template, FIFO drain, deletion, maxSpillBytes enforcement, stale-file guard) and concurrency_protocol (AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> CAS hot-swap within partition lock, bounded BLOCK park, per-edge drain serialization, drain-before-switch guard). All 11 affected_surfaces map to at least one slice's allowed_paths. No slice contains an entry that appears in both its own allowed_paths and forbidden_paths. Every implementer and both QA slices carry verification commands (qa/smoke.sh and/or qa/regression.sh). The acceptance_test_matrix covers stale spill on startup, CRC/length invariant failure, and failure/partial-write recovery — satisfying the three lifecycle sub-cases. topology is split_specialists with two implementer slices, which is compatible (SINGLE topology would be the violation). A reviewer slice (engineering.review) is present. engineering.qa.author precedes both implementers in the dependency chain. engineering.qa.verify follows the review slice. QA author/verify allowed paths are strictly in src/test/ and qa/fixtures/ trees, fully disjoint from implementer src/main/ paths. Every non-terminal slice is consumed by a downstream slice; no orphans exist. finalization_policy is open_final_feature_pr_for_human_merge, keeping merge human-gated. All slice objectives name concrete files, test class names, method signatures, and metrics. The risk_register carries 12 explicit entries. R-006 has no external roadmap dependencies ('Depends on: none'); the MmapJournal soft dependency is sequenced internally via the design slice gate. The zero-allocation hard constraint is stated in design_contract.hard_constraints, enforced by the jmhSmokeCheck acceptance gate, and repeated in impl-policy-core's objective — no scheduled work violates it. R-006 spans 11 affected surfaces with four policy variants, mmap I/O integration, and hot-swap; 6 slices under split_specialists topology is proportionate and not excessive for this complexity.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge carries an AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> for hot-swap; swap is a single CAS. Queue-length check and policy dispatch execute under the existing per-partition lock to prevent torn reads. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free reads against queue capacity within the partition lock scope. BLOCK policy uses the partition lock's Condition to park the producer thread; a bounded park timeout (configurable, default 100 ms) prevents indefinite deadlock; BLOCK must not share a lock with the consumer read path. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes and drain through a per-edge lock; drain holds the partition lock and blocks concurrent appends. Hot-swap waits for any active spill drain to complete before activating the new policy.
forbidden_alternatives: New or custom spill file format bypassing MmapJournal.
Global (non-per-edge) policy applied uniformly without Builder opt-in.
Cross-partition backpressure signaling.
Priority queues or weighted shedding inside DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
Persistent spill recovery across JVM restarts.
Custom policy SPI or user-supplied BackpressurePolicy implementations.
Mutable EdgeBackpressureConfig fields mutated in place for hot-swap.
Merging BackpressurePolicy into the existing JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy enums.
hard_constraints: Reuse MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc for all spill I/O; do not invent a new binary format.
Allocation gate (jmhSmokeCheck) must remain green; no per-event heap allocation on the hot path for DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, or BLOCK when queue is not full.
No custom policy extension point (no BackpressurePolicy interface or SPI beyond the four specified values).
No priority-based shedding within DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
No cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Hot-swap must not lose records already committed to the spill file; drain completes before the new policy activates.
EdgeBackpressureConfig must be immutable; policy hot-swap goes through setEdgeBackpressure only.
BackpressurePolicy must be a standalone enum; do not merge with JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy.
BLOCK policy must not share a lock with the consumer read path to avoid deadlock.
R-002/MmapJournal API availability must be confirmed by the design slice before impl-overflow-spill proceeds.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns BackpressurePolicy enum and EdgeBackpressureConfig value type with no runtime imports. runtime-core owns per-edge policy enforcement, DROP/BLOCK queue-overflow dispatch, spill lifecycle, and hot-swap implementation. dag-framework-lvc MmapJournal is consumed read-only by runtime-core via a MmapSpillAdapter wrapper; no modifications to dag-framework-lvc internals. QA write paths own all test fixtures, failing tests, and regression scripts exclusively.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK uses MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc as the spill backend. Spill file path: <tempdir>/dag-spill-<partitionId>-<edgeId>.spill. Journal is append-only during overflow; drained in arrival order (FIFO) when the edge queue drops below half-capacity. Spill file is deleted via MmapJournal.close() after full drain. EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes is enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter. No cross-restart recovery; a stale spill file on startup triggers IllegalStateException before partition starts, not silent replay.
design_contract.public_api: New enum BackpressurePolicy { DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, OVERFLOW_TO_DISK } in dag-framework-api/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/dag/api/BackpressurePolicy.java. EdgeBackpressureConfig immutable record (BackpressurePolicy policy, int capacity, Path spillDir, long maxSpillBytes) in dag-framework-api/src/main/java/com/joshorig/ull/dag/api/EdgeBackpressureConfig.java. GraphDefinitionBuilder gains addEdgeBackpressure(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy). GraphPartitionRunner.Builder gains edgeBackpressure(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy policy) and edgeBackpressure(String edgeId, EdgeBackpressureConfig config). Running runner exposes setEdgeBackpressure(String edgeId, BackpressurePolicy policy) for hot-swap.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge carries an AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> for hot-swap; swap is a single CAS. Queue-length check and policy dispatch execute under the existing per-partition lock to prevent torn reads. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free reads against queue capacity within the partition lock scope. BLOCK policy uses the partition lock's Condition to park the producer thread; a bounded park timeout (configurable, default 100 ms) prevents indefinite deadlock; BLOCK must not share a lock with the consumer read path. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes and drain through a per-edge lock; drain holds the partition lock and blocks concurrent appends. Hot-swap waits for any active spill drain to complete before activating the new policy.
forbidden_alternatives: New or custom spill file format bypassing MmapJournal.
Global (non-per-edge) policy applied uniformly without Builder opt-in.
Cross-partition backpressure signaling.
Priority queues or weighted shedding inside DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
Persistent spill recovery across JVM restarts.
Custom policy SPI or user-supplied BackpressurePolicy implementations.
Mutable EdgeBackpressureConfig fields mutated in place for hot-swap.
Merging BackpressurePolicy into the existing JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy enums.
hard_constraints: Reuse MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc for all spill I/O; do not invent a new binary format.
Allocation gate (jmhSmokeCheck) must remain green; no per-event heap allocation on the hot path for DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, or BLOCK when queue is not full.
No custom policy extension point (no BackpressurePolicy interface or SPI beyond the four specified values).
No priority-based shedding within DROP_NEW or DROP_OLD.
No cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Hot-swap must not lose records already committed to the spill file; drain completes before the new policy activates.
EdgeBackpressureConfig must be immutable; policy hot-swap goes through setEdgeBackpressure only.
BackpressurePolicy must be a standalone enum; do not merge with JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy.
BLOCK policy must not share a lock with the consumer read path to avoid deadlock.
R-002 (MmapJournal) must be merged and present in dag-framework-lvc before impl-overflow-spill begins; impl-overflow-spill must not implement an alternative spill format if R-002 is absent.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns BackpressurePolicy enum and EdgeBackpressureConfig value type with no runtime imports. runtime-core owns per-edge policy enforcement, DROP/BLOCK queue-overflow dispatch, spill lifecycle, and hot-swap implementation. dag-framework-lvc MmapJournal is consumed read-only by runtime-core via a MmapSpillAdapter wrapper; no modifications to dag-framework-lvc internals. QA write paths own all test fixtures, failing tests, and regression scripts exclusively.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK uses MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc as the spill backend. Spill file path: <tempdir>/dag-spill-<partitionId>-<edgeId>.spill. Journal is append-only during overflow; drained in arrival order (FIFO) when the edge queue drops below half-capacity. Spill file is deleted via MmapJournal.close() after full drain. EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes is enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter. No cross-restart recovery; a stale spill file on startup triggers IllegalStateException before partition starts, not silent replay.

design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge carries an AtomicReference<BackpressurePolicy> for hot-swap; swap is a single CAS. Queue-length check and policy dispatch execute under the existing per-partition lock to prevent torn reads. DROP_NEW and DROP_OLD are lock-free reads against queue capacity within the partition lock scope. BLOCK policy uses the partition lock's Condition to park the producer thread; a bounded park timeout (configurable, default 100 ms) prevents indefinite deadlock; BLOCK must not share a lock with the consumer read path. OVERFLOW_TO_DISK serializes spill writes and drain through a per-edge lock; drain holds the partition lock and blocks concurrent appends. Hot-swap waits for any active spill drain to complete before activating the new policy.

Cross-partition backpressure signaling.

Persistent spill recovery across JVM restarts.
Custom policy SPI or user-supplied BackpressurePolicy implementations.
Mutable EdgeBackpressureConfig fields mutated in place for hot-swap.

EdgeBackpressureConfig must be immutable; policy hot-swap goes through setEdgeBackpressure only.
BackpressurePolicy must be a standalone enum; do not merge with JoinPolicy or PartitionPolicy.
BLOCK policy must not share a lock with the consumer read path to avoid deadlock.

design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK uses MmapJournal from dag-framework-lvc as the spill backend. Spill file path: <tempdir>/dag-spill-<partitionId>-<edgeId>.spill. risk_register: MmapJournal API surface in dag-framework-lvc may not expose append/drain/close at the granularity needed; mitigation: design slice must confirm API fit before qa-author writes tests.

Hot-swap CAS between policy-read and queue-mutation under concurrent producer threads may allow one record to observe stale policy; mitigation: AtomicReference read and queue dispatch must be within the same partition lock critical section.

BLOCK policy deadlock if consumer never catches up or consumer and producer share a thread pool; mitigation: bounded park with timeout (default 100 ms) and dropped-block metric; document thread-safety contract; test explicitly on separate threads in qa-author.

Spill file not deleted on JVM crash leaves stale file on next startup; mitigation: stale file startup guard throws IllegalStateException; register JVM shutdown hook in MmapSpillAdapter to close and unmap the segment; operator must delete manually (no silent replay).

Allocation regression on hot path: spill coordinator instantiation, AtomicReference boxing, or per-edge lock allocation may trigger GC; mitigation: allocate lock objects once at Builder.build() time; allocation gate in jmhSmokeCheck is a hard acceptance gate.
Drain ordering under concurrent append: simultaneous overflow and drain may interleave records; mitigation: drain holds partition lock; appends are blocked during drain.
MmapJournal close race if hot-swap fires while drain is in progress; mitigation: hot-swap guard waits for active drain to complete before switching policy.

Spill file not cleaned up on abnormal partition close (OOM, uncaught exception); mitigation: try-finally in partition lifecycle; reviewer must confirm cleanup path is covered by the OVERFLOW_TO_DISK failure/partial-write acceptance test.

Unbounded spill file growth if drain rate is permanently below fill rate; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig.maxSpillBytes enforced at write time; overflow beyond maxSpillBytes falls back to DROP_NEW and increments a spill-overflow counter.

MmapJournal API version mismatch between lvc-standard pinned in dag-framework-lvc and the spill adapter call sites; mitigation: compile-time module dependency on dag-framework-lvc; integration test in qa-verify will surface API breakage.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK spill directory not writable at runtime; mitigation: EdgeBackpressureConfig validation at Builder.build() must throw IllegalArgumentException for non-writable spillDir.

R-002/snapshot sequencing risk: if a future iteration gates R-006 on R-002, MmapJournal availability must be re-confirmed; mitigation: design DECISIONS.md entry explicitly records R-006 independence from R-002; reviewer must confirm no lvc API is missing at review time.
